newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Yen stampede sidelines dollar bulls.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Yen stampede sidelines dollar bulls.

text.p: The yen continued its broad-based climb up the charts, leaving the dollar and most other currencies struggling to contain the damage, technical analysts said on Monday.
The rapid pace of dollar/yen's overnight descent suggests more losses lie ahead, with a test of lows posted near 110.50 in June and last November now likely, chartists said.
"The impulsive nature of the downleg from 114.15 suggests a retest of the lows," said Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy in Montreal.
The dollar fell from its session high at 114.16 yen to as low as 111.98 in Asian trading before recovering somewhat during U.S. morning trade.
The yen also gained on the mark, pound, Swiss franc and Australian dollar, demonstrating the power of its current advance, chartists said.
"The yen crosses are heavy across the board. They are all pressured and likely to head lower," said Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Mark/yen fell to a 23-month low at 64.22 before stabilizing while the Aussie dollar fell two yen overnight.
"We had a previous mark/yen low at 64.55 that got broken convincingly overnight. A daily close below there looks very nice for a continuation of the downleg," said Autotte.
The dollar lost a pfennig-and-a-half overnight but regained much of that deficit on the back of the mark/yen weakness, chartists said.
New York trade saw the eclipse of a barrier at 1.7480 marks that had restrained the dollar overnight, though the momentum in dollar/mark still leans lower, analysts said.
"This is the first trading day in the last eight where dollar/mark posted a lower low and lower high," Spain said.
"We have a (dollar/mark) correction on our hands which is still incomplete," Spain added.
Still, recapturing 1.7480 marks should help the dollar stave off any imminent tests of last Monday's low at 1.7350, technicians said.
Sterling/mark's rebound may have helped bolster dollar/mark in U.S. trade, analysts said.
The pound had pulled back three pfennigs from its post-UK budget highs approaching 2.97, but steadily crawled back above 2.95.
